newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ivory Coast in debt reduction deal.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast in debt reduction deal.

text.p: Ivory Coast signed an accord on Tuesday with the London Club of creditor banks allowing it to slash its external commercial debt to $2.6 billion from $6.8 billion.
The signing, which followed two years of negotiations, came after a preliminary agreement reached on November 22 which was the subject of roadshow presentations to creditors at the start of February.

Prior to the restructuring, the debt outstanding to London Club creditors totalled $2.4 billion in principal and $4.4 billion in interest racked up since April 1987 when the world's leading cocoa producer ceased payments.
Talks on the agreement started in October 1995.
The signing in Paris was attended by Ivory Coast finance minister N'Goran Niamien who called the accord a vote of "great confidence in Ivory Coast's economic and financial prospects.
Ivory Coast will purchase 30 percent of the outstanding principal at a price of 24 percent of face value, with related interest to be erased.
It will then exchange the remaining principal with its creditors who will have two choices.

The creditors can take 20-year front-loaded interest reduction bonds (FLIRBS) repayable in 21 semi-annual installments with a 9.5 year grace period, or 30-year discount bonds of 50 percent repayable at maturity to be guaranteed by zero-coupon government bonds of equal maturity.

Thierry Desjardins of Banque Nationale de Paris, who was head of the steering commmittee of London Club creditors, said the preference of most creditor banks for FLIRBS -- debt instruments without a guaratee of reimbursement of the capital -- underlined the confidence in the country's prospects.
Ivory Coast expects to hold talks this month with the International Monetary Fund on a new three-year programme of IMF-backed reforms.

The IMF agreed last month to widen guidelines on which countries qualify to benefit from a new debt relief initiative being carried out jointly with the World Bank and Paris Club of creditor nations to help poor heavily-indebted nations.
The Ivory Coast has not said how much money would be involved in the new debt relief.
